Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise methods card for the historical churn archive describing how H2 was intended to be tested before its ruling. Clearly label it as historical setup rather than a current conclusion.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Historical Churn Archive — H2 Methods Card", "folder": "historical churn archive", "body": "HISTORICAL SETUP — NOT A CURRENT CONCLUSION

Purpose
Test whether the H2 mid-segment churn increase could be explained by ordinary February seasonality or a competitor-cycle effect, before issuing the H2 ruling.

Intended test
- Recreate the same cohort logic used in the January scan.
- Apply Owen’s validation/check to the cohort construction and denominator handling.
- Compare same-window February mid-segment monthly churn for the current read with February 2021 and February 2022.
- Keep segment definitions, observation window, churn measure, and denominator treatment consistent across years.
- Overlay only market or competitor events with an actual timestamp; do not infer a competitor effect from untimestamped “noise.”
- Keep Marcus’s pricing-page experiment separate; it was not part of this historical comparison.

Pre-ruling quality gate
Complete one final denominator-handling sanity check before locking the interpretation. If the historical corpus or comparable snapshots were unavailable, mark the test inconclusive rather than treating missing data as evidence.

Historical record of the intended read
The eventual comparison recorded February 2021 and 2022 mid-segment churn at approximately 2.0%–2.2%, with no matching spike under the same cohort logic. That belongs to the historical ruling record; this card documents how H2 was intended to be tested and is not a current churn conclusion."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_049_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The card presents H2's historical test plan, not a final conclusion. Purpose

- Recreate the same cohort logic used in the January scan.

- Compare same-window February mid-segment monthly churn for the current read with February 2021 and February 2022.
- Keep segment definitions, observation window, churn measure, and denominator treatment consistent across years.
- Overlay only market or competitor events with an actual timestamp; do not infer a competitor effect from untimestamped “noise.”
- Keep Marcus’s pricing-page experiment separate; it was not part of this historical comparison.
